issue.body:
### Description

I get `invalid device ordinal` errors when oversubscribing GPUs on a SLURM cluster.

For example, this script starts a job over 2 nodes (each having 4 GPUs), with 8 tasks per node (2 tasks per GPU):

```bash
#!/bin/bash -l
#SBATCH --time=00:05:00
#SBATCH --nodes=2
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=8
#SBATCH --constraint=gpu
#SBATCH --gpus-per-node=4
#SBATCH --gpu-bind=none

export XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE=false

srun python3 my_jax_script.py
```

SLURM assigns `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` properly (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3`), and other GPU frameworks run fine, but I run into the following error when my JAX script hits `jax.distributed.initialize()`:

```
W external/xla/xla/service/platform_util.cc:206] unable to create StreamExecutor for CUDA:6: CUDA error: Failed call to cuDeviceGet: CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_DEVICE: invalid device ordinal
```

The error happens on 4 tasks, `CUDA:4` to `CUDA:7`, which makes me believe that JAX is looking for (non-existent) devices 4 to 7.


### System info (python version, jaxlib version, accelerator, etc.)

The script is run on GPU nodes of the [Perlmutter supercomputer](https://docs.nersc.gov/systems/perlmutter/architecture/) which each have 4 A100 GPU and one AMD EPYC 7763 CPU.
